summary: Interpreted the revised transfer receipt (23acf06d8a524b2790ef674d5eb04cb0): all six comparisons hold, and the liveness half is now measured rather than inferred — in the non-voter case the previous leader was outside Leader state in all 1289 samples from the instant of the call, 241 samples found no leader at all (first 1ms, last 278ms after the call, about 1.4 election timeouts against a 200ms timeout), the maximum term rose 2 to 4, leadership ended on a voter other than the requested target, and the call had already returned nil, while the voter-target control recorded a completed transfer. The account stays scoped to the wrong success report plus the observed bounded interruption, with no data-loss claim. The gap about the interruption is resolved, and the measured disruption is promoted as a new Fact (@transfer_nonvoter_disruption) with both receipts cited. Remaining work: the identity of the successor is timing dependent (the two receipts differed) and is recorded only; and a read of the live-bootstrap path (liveBootstrap, BootstrapCluster, HasExistingState) surfaced no defect — HasExistingState rejects a node with a persisted term — so no new suspicion was registered from it.
